prompt: Summarize why gradient checkpointing helps train large models on small GPUs.
base_response:
Gradient checkpointing helps train large models on small GPUs by storing the gradients of the model parameters, rather than the parameters themselves. This is done by periodically saving the gradients to disk, allowing the model to be trained on smaller GPUs and enabling faster training on more powerful GPUs. This technique reduces the memory requirements for training large models on small GPUs, making it possible to train these models efficiently.
